method: SF3D's remesh normally only runs inside run_image, which would re-run the network and bake a texture. Mesh.triangle_remesh and Mesh.quad_remesh are pure geometry operations, so the existing GLB was wrapped back into an SF3D Mesh and remeshed with no second inference pass.

comparison.vs_raw_sf3d: Both remeshes are a large topology win: max triangle aspect 704.6 -> 1.7 (triangle) and -> 2.7 (quad), extreme-aspect triangles 246 -> 0, with roughly half the triangles. The 11% Z-extent loss is the spikes being trimmed, not hull damage; the silhouette is otherwise unchanged.
comparison.vs_mini_turbo_candidate_2: SF3D remeshed topology is far cleaner than Mini Turbo's (max aspect 1.7 vs 132916, 0 vs 6780 extreme-aspect triangles), but Mini Turbo is the only one of the two that is actually the ship. Clean topology on a collapsed pod does not beat usable geometry.
comparison.vs_pymeshlab_cleanup: PyMeshLab cleanup is conservative repair and leaves the triangle distribution alone; SF3D remeshing rebuilds it isotropically and gets a far better aspect profile. They are not interchangeable: remeshing needs an SF3D Mesh, cleanup works on any GLB.

usability_verdict: Remeshing is proven useful as a technique and would be the right post-step if SF3D ever reconstructs this subject. It does not change SF3D's HARD_REJECT on the ship.
